title: Atropine (0.05%) for rapid progressive childhood myopia (ARM study)

license.statement: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 License); private

groups.description: atropine 0.05% eye drops in both eyes once at bedtime for 1 year with single-vision spectacles; single arm, AIIMS New Delhi, India; treatment-naive children with documented progression > 0.75 D in the preceding year (pre-treatment criterion); mean age of the 40 enrolled children from the Results text

series.notes: mean ± SD; both eyes pooled per child (Methods: clustered data of both eyes pooled with robust standard errors), used as tabulated; n = 40 = all enrolled children (Table 1 heading); 12 months = '1 year on atropine'

exclusions.what: T1 spherical equivalent and rate-of-progression rows, including the '1 year before treatment' column
exclusions.reason: not axial length (protocol inclusion 1); the pre-treatment column has no axial length

exclusions.what: T2 subgroups by gender, age (6–9, 10–12 years) and parental myopia
exclusions.reason: myopia progression in dioptres only, no axial length (protocol inclusion 1); only the whole cohort has axial length, so it is extracted

exclusions.what: T3 groups by treatment response (progression < 0.5 D vs ≥ 0.5 D per year on atropine)
exclusions.reason: groups selected by a post-treatment outcome (protocol inclusion 5); no axial length

exclusions.what: AL change after 1 year reported in the Results text
exclusions.reason: not a table cell; the absolute series of T1 is used

notes: Prospective interventional single-arm trial registered in India (Institute Ethics Committee IEC552/2022), children aged 6–12 years, SER −2 to −6 D, astigmatism ≤ 1.5 D, documented progression > 0.75 D in the preceding year; no prior myopia control.
AL by partial coherence interferometry (IOLMaster 700, Carl Zeiss Meditec AG); units mm (T1 row label).
Methods mention linear mixed-effect models to address missing data at random; T1 gives mean ± SD for all 40 enrolled children and is read as raw means (no missing data reported).
Follow-up visits at 6 and 12 months; cycloplegic refraction (SER) is tabulated and not used.
